POL-NS-21 sets a 300 s free wait that, on an on-demand trip, runs from the driver's arrival; the auto-arrival event places the driver at the pickup at 10:37:25, so the wait ended at 10:42:25 (trip_record.derived.v7.free_wait.ends_at). The driver cancelled at 10:42:10 — 285 s from arrival, 15 s short (trip_record.derived.v7.free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait = false, seconds_from_start_to_cancel = 285.0). POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition is not met, so no no-show fee may stand against the rider and no compensation may issue to the driver.

The arrival clock is fixed by the trace, and it fails the driver on either available start point. POL-NS-21's arrival test is corroborated on this record: the nearest GPS fix to the pickup is 3.99 m away, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, at 5 m reported accuracy (gps_trace.derived.v7.arrival_check.corroborated = true), and the trace shows the vehicle stationary at speed 0 from 10:37:30 through 10:42:00. Measured from the arrival event (10:37:25) the 300 s wait ends at 10:42:25; measured from the platform's own wait timer (started 10:37:30) it ends at 10:42:30. The cancellation at 10:42:10 is early on both readings, so the driver cannot bring himself inside POL-NS-22 by pointing to his own timer.

The rider does not contend that the driver breached POL-NS-23. On this record the driver sent two in-app messages (MSG-06054-001 at 10:37:50, MSG-06054-002 at 10:40:20) and placed one in-app call (10:41:05, unanswered, ringing 18 s), all before the 10:42:10 cancellation, so the message-and-call obligation is satisfied (trip_record.derived.v7.contact_before_cancel.obligation_met = true) and the fee does not fall on that clause. The rider's case rests on the timing of the cancellation, not on contact.

The rider's account is the one the record bears out. Her statement was that the driver 'cancelled before I could even get to the lift lobby, it was less than 5 minutes'; the derived interval from arrival to cancellation is 285 s, under five minutes, and the trace shows the driver had been at the pickup only 4 minutes 45 seconds when he cancelled. Nothing in the trip record, the trace, or the chat log contradicts her, and the driver's own profile and history are not a ground of decision on this trip (POL-GEN-01).

The contested 5.00 SGD is already back with the rider and was recovered from the driver at 11:17:10 after her complaint (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, fee_reversed event); the driver filed to undo that state. Because the cancellation was 15 s premature, the driver's claim is not supported and the present state stands. Under POL-GEN-03 that is NO_ACTION - never 'restore a charge' - so no driver_compensation_sgd may issue and the rider keeps the 5.00 SGD. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence and no value-based escalation arises.

There is no open question here that would force escalation under POL-GEN-26, and the rider asks the AI to decide rather than hold the fee. The only missing artifact is a third-party traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-06054-01, which is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and which carries no fact; it is impaired and the rider does not present it as clean. No no-show rule needs a traffic fact. Every fact POL-NS-21 to POL-NS-23 require - arrival time, wait elapsed, contact attempted, and the moment of cancellation - is carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no fact 'the record cannot establish'.

claims.text: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the face of the record: he sent two in-app chat messages (10:37:50 and 10:40:20, read by the rider at 10:38:34 and 10:40:50) and placed an in-app call at 10:41:05 (unanswered, rang 18 s), all before the 10:42:10 cancellation, so the clause that voids the fee for want of contact is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND can rest on it.

The driver arrived at the pickup and his arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace: the trip record's arrival event at 10:37:25 is corroborated (arrival_check.corroborated = true), with a fix 3.99 m from the pickup at 10:39:00, inside the 50 m arrival radius for this STANDARD pickup zone, so POL-NS-24's premise (a driver who failed to arrive) is absent and neither its full refund nor its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is available against the driver.

The driver waited at the pickup rather than leaving it: the driver-device trace carries 22 fixes at 30 s intervals with 100% coverage and no gap exceeding 30 s, and every fix from 10:37:30 through 10:42:00 reports zero speed at the pickup point, so the driver was physically present and holding for the rider for the whole of the free-wait window.

The sum in issue is exactly the policy figure, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount check or referral arises: the ledger carries a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line that reconciles to total_charged, fee_matches_policy is true, and the derived money block puts the fee charged, the policy fee and the driver's compensation if upheld all at 5.00 SGD.

Each step POL-NS-21 lays down for a no-show cancellation was followed in substance: arrival at 10:37:25, first message at 10:37:50, a call at 10:41:05, a second message at 10:40:20, and cancellation at 10:42:10 - 285 s of the 300 s free wait. The 15-second margin off the full free wait engages no clause of POLICY-NO-SHOW: the only grounds the policy gives to void the fee (POL-NS-23, want of contact) and to refund it (POL-NS-24, failure to arrive) are both absent here, and POL-NS-21 attaches no monetary penalty of its own to a premature cancellation, so the fee charged under POL-NS-22 stands and is the driver's compensation.

The present state is provisional, not a determination: the fee was reversed at 11:17:10 only as an 'Interim reversal after a rider complaint ... pending review', so nothing on the record adjudicates that the fee was wrongly charged. Under POL-NS-22 the fee charged to the rider is transferred to the driver as compensation, and because the driver is the filer, POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION merely leave that complaint-driven refund standing against him; DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00 SGD is the outcome that gives the driver the fee the policy provides.

No fact a no-show rule needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26's escalation gate is not open: the only absent artifact is the traffic advisory, which is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 and therefore carries no fact, and no clause of POLICY-NO-SHOW requires a traffic advisory. The no-show question can be decided on this record.

The ruling on this no-show is one the AI may make finally: the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (driver_profile.fraud_flags = 0, rider_profile.fraud_flags = 0), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the required confidence is 0.0 and the case should be decided now rather than sent to a human reviewer.

ruling.explanation:
Decision: NO_ACTION. The 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider stays with her and is not recovered for the driver; both amount fields are null, and no referral arises. Because the driver filed, the question is whether his claim against the present state is supported, and it is not.

Everything turns on one fact: whether the driver cancelled after the free wait. Under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait on this on-demand trip runs from the driver's arrival, and the auto-arrival event and the corroborated GPS trace fix that at 10:37:25 (EV-TRIP-06054; EV-GPS-06054, both weight 1.0, COMPLETE), so the wait ended at 10:42:25. The cancellation was logged at 10:42:10 — 285 s after arrival, 15 s short (trip_record.derived.v7.free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait = false). POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee and its transfer to the driver as compensation only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition was not met, so no fee was chargeable and none is owed to the driver. The driver's point that POL-NS-21 attaches no separate monetary penalty to a premature cancellation is right but does not help him: this is not a penalty on the driver, it is the fee's own precondition, and the precondition failed. The rider's account ('less than 5 minutes') is what the record bears out.

The driver's remaining points do not change this. The contact obligation in POL-NS-23 was met — two in-app messages (10:37:50 and 10:40:20) and one unanswered in-app call (10:41:05), all before the 10:42:10 cancellation, as both sides accept — so POL-NS-23 does not void the fee; equally it does not revive it. POL-NS-24 is not engaged: the driver did arrive (a GPS fix 3.99 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius), so there is no driver no-show and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit referral. The 11:17:10 reversal was recorded as interim, but POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION the outcome where the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, and it never means 'restore a charge'.

No escalation: the only missing artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06054-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0), carries no fact any no-show clause needs, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final. No referral clause fires: the fee is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy figure, so the POL-NS-22 fee-amount check does not fire; the driver did arrive, so POL-NS-24's credit does not fire; and the rider's repeat no-show field is not present in the profile and the fee does not stand, so POL-NS-25 does not fire.

Confidence is 0.95, against a cap of 1.0 — the deciding facts are carried by EV-TRIP-06054 and EV-GPS-06054, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — and the bar under POL-GEN-22 / POL-NS-26 is 0.0.

The driver filed to undo the 5.00 SGD refund already issued to the rider and recovered from him. On the record, that refund is correct and the driver's claim fails, so the present state stands (NO_ACTION) and no money moves in either direction.

Why the fee cannot stand: POL-NS-21 sets a free wait of 300 s (5 minutes) which, on this on-demand trip, runs from the driver's arrival. The platform's arrival event, corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace (nearest fix 3.99 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, accuracy 5 m), puts the driver at the pickup at 10:37:25, so the free wait ended at 10:42:25 (the platform's own wait timer started at 10:37:30 and would have ended at 10:42:30). The driver cancelled at 10:42:10, 285 s after arrival — 15 s short on either reading, and trip_record.derived.v7.free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait is false. POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD no-show fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'; that condition is not met, so the fee was not authorised. The 5.00 SGD was reversed at 11:17:10 (fare ledger payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00) and the rider keeps it.

The driver's arguments, and what they meet: the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was satisfied — two in-app messages (MSG-06054-001 at 10:37:50, MSG-06054-002 at 10:40:20) and one in-app call (10:41:05, unanswered, 18 s) all before the 10:42:10 cancellation — so no FULL_REFUND arises on that clause; I accept that, and it does not cure the timing. The arrival was corroborated and the driver waited stationary at the pickup throughout the window (22 fixes, 30 s spacing, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s), so POL-NS-24's premise (a driver who never arrived) is absent and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is owed. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy figure (fee_matches_policy = true), so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check produces no referral. I reject the argument that POL-NS-21 carries no monetary consequence of its own: POL-NS-22 makes 'after the free wait' the very condition of the fee, so a cancellation 15 s early leaves no fee to transfer to the driver, and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION can follow. I also reject the suggestion that the reversal is only provisional and therefore no adjudication: the record shows the charge the policy does not authorise, and the driver bears the burden of showing the fee was due.

No escalation: the only absent artifact is the third-party traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06054-01 (status MISSING, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), which carries no fact and is not required by any no-show clause, so POL-GEN-26 is not open. No safety flag (POL-GEN-21) is present. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party carries a fraud flag (driver 0, rider 0), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at the required confidence of 0.0; the deciding facts are carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown), giving a confidence cap of 1.0. POL-NS-25 produces no referral: the count it reads (rider no-show cancellations in 30 days) is not present on the rider profile, and in any event the fee does not stand. No other clause produces a referral.

To driver D-77741 and rider R-59466: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee does not stand, so the driver's claim to be paid it fails and the present state — the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 11:17:10 — remains. This was an on-demand trip, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 10:37:25 and would have ended at 10:42:25. The driver cancelled at 10:42:10, i.e. 285 seconds after arrival and 15 seconds before the wait expired (trip_record free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait = false, seconds_from_start_to_cancel = 285.0). POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'; that condition was not met, so the fee had no basis and the rider was correctly refunded. The driver's other points are accepted but do not change this: he did arrive (arrival event 10:37:25 corroborated by the trace, nearest fix 3.99 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and he did meet his contact obligation under POL-NS-23 (chat messages at 10:37:50 and 10:40:20, in-app call at 10:41:05, all before cancellation). Those findings only matter if the fee was validly charged, and it was not; POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 are therefore not engaged, but neither can rescue a fee whose precondition failed. The driver's argument that the 15-second margin carries no monetary penalty is rejected: POL-NS-22's own words make cancellation after the free wait the condition on which the fee and the transfer to the driver depend, and POL-NS-21 attaches no authority to cancel as a no-show before the wait has run. Because the driver is the filer and the rider is owed the refund already issued, POL-GEN-03 gives NO_ACTION, with both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd null; this is not a partial refund, it simply leaves the rider's 5.00 SGD where it is. The amount in issue (5.00 SGD) is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the ruling is final at any confidence. No referral arises: the fee charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral; the driver arrived and made contact so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit; and the rider's repeat-no-show counter is not present and the fee does not stand, so no POL-NS-25 flag. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06054-01, weight 0.0) carries no fact any no-show rule needs, so POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation. Confidence is capped at 1.0, the weight of the trip record and GPS trace that carry the deciding facts.
